name: Path of the Oni
introduction: To walk the Path of the Oni is to be unsatisfied, always hungry for more of whatever compulsions drive the barbarian: food, pleasure, combat, etc... The barbarian begins this path when the blood of a ravenous oni awakens inside of them, they are cursed with an oni’s essence, or they have a near-death experience at one’s hands and incorporates part of their nature. Or, in a more grim fashion, if one is taught the ways of life and combat by an oni directly.

blocks.text: You can read, write, and speak both Giant and Abyssal, and have Expertise in Athletics or Intimidation checks (your choice when gaining this feature).

You can channel the fiendish giant’s power imbued in your body to grow to absurd heights. When you Rage, you can choose to produce the enlarge effects of enlarge/reduce targeting yourself, requiring no concentration or spell slot and these effects are not treated as a spell or magical effect. They are produced as though cast at a level equal to half your barbarian level (rounded up, maximum 9th) or lower (you choose). These effects end when your Rage does.
You can choose to produce this effect a number of times per Long Rest equal to your proficiency bonus.
You can replicate an oni’s ability to levitate, and have a belabored flight (hover) speed equal to your base movement speed.

Your body can stitch itself back together as needed. When you begin your turn with 1 or more hit points, but no more than half your hit point maximum remains, you regain hit points equal to a d6 + your proficiency bonus.
Your mastery of a ravenous giant’s nature grows, allowing you the following the improvements on your previous features:

When you use Titan’s Wrath to enlarge but your Rage ends, you can choose to continue the effects of enlarge/reduce, but must begin concentrating on those effects, which end either when you stop concentrating or 1 minute passes.
When you are Raging, your belabored flight (hover) speed becomes a hover (flight) speed instead.
When you make any attack that you have advantage on and hit, you may roll one additional weapon damage die and add it to the damage result.
